authority: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (via oil marketing companies — IOC, BPC, HPC)

description.en: Application for a new LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) connection through oil marketing companies — Indian Oil Corporation (Indane), Bharat Petroleum (Bharatgas), or Hindustan Petroleum (HP Gas). Also covers the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) which provides free LPG connections to eligible BPL (Below Poverty Line) families.

verifiedConditions.claim: Only one LPG connection is allowed per household. The applicant's household must not have an existing LPG connection with any oil marketing company. This is verified through the linked Aadhaar and address details.

PM Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) connections are available to women belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) families as identified by the SECC (Socio Economic Caste Census) data, or belonging to SC/ST households, beneficiaries of PMAY, AAY, forest dwellers, most backward classes, tea/ex-tea garden tribes, or residents of islands and river islands.

unverifiedEligibility: Regular (non-Ujjwala) connections are available to any adult citizen with valid KYC documents, subject to one connection per household.
Existing connection holders can apply for a transfer or name change but not a second connection at the same address.

requirements.claim: A duly filled KYC (Know Your Customer) form with the applicant's details must be submitted. The form is available at the distributor's office or can be downloaded from the oil marketing company's website.
Identity proof such as Aadhaar card, voter ID, passport, or driving license is required. Aadhaar is mandatory for subsidy transfer through PAHAL (DBTL) scheme.
Address proof such as Aadhaar card, voter ID, electricity bill, or ration card matching the address where the connection is sought.
Recent passport-size photograph of the applicant is required.
For PM Ujjwala Yojana applicants, SECC ration card or BPL certificate as per eligible categories is required to verify eligibility under the scheme.
Bank account details (passbook or cancelled cheque) are required for LPG subsidy transfer under the PAHAL (DBTL) scheme. The bank account must be linked with Aadhaar.

processInformation.claim: The process involves: (1) Visit the nearest LPG distributor (Indane/Bharatgas/HP Gas) or apply online through the MyLPG portal or oil marketing company's website, (2) Submit KYC form with required documents, (3) Pay the applicable fees (security deposit for cylinder and regulator, and cost of first refill), (4) For Ujjwala applicants, the connection is provided free of charge — only the cost of the first refill may be borne by the applicant or can be recovered from future subsidy, (5) Distributor verifies documents and schedules delivery, (6) Delivery of cylinder, regulator, and gas stove (for Ujjwala) to the registered address.
doesNotEstablish: This record does not establish cylinder delivery schedules or refill waiting times.
This record does not cover the PAHAL subsidy calculation or payout timelines.

output.claim: An active LPG connection with a consumer number, including a 14.2 kg LPG cylinder, pressure regulator, and delivery of the first refill. Ujjwala beneficiaries also receive a free gas stove.

fees.applicability: Regular new LPG connection (Rs. 1,600-2,200 approximately for security deposit + regulator + first cylinder)
fees.claim: For a regular (non-Ujjwala) new LPG connection, the cost includes a refundable security deposit for the cylinder (approximately Rs. 1,250-1,450), regulator charge, and the cost of the first gas refill. Total initial cost is approximately Rs. 1,600 to Rs. 2,200 depending on the oil marketing company and current cylinder price.

fees.applicability: PM Ujjwala Yojana — free LPG connection for eligible BPL families
fees.claim: Under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY), the LPG connection is provided completely free of charge. The government bears the cost of the cylinder security deposit, pressure regulator, and a free gas stove. The cost of the first refill may be borne by the beneficiary or recovered from future LPG subsidy.

processingTime.applicability: New LPG connection from application to delivery
processingTime.claim: New LPG connections are typically processed and delivered within 7 to 15 days of application and document verification, subject to distributor availability and logistics.

limitations: This record covers new domestic LPG connections; commercial connections have different processes and higher charges.
Cylinder prices and security deposits are revised periodically by oil marketing companies and may differ from the amounts mentioned.
Ujjwala scheme eligibility is based on SECC data and government-defined categories which may be updated.
Distributor availability varies by location; waiting times depend on local demand.
This record does not cover LPG connection transfer, surrender, or double-bottle scheme.
Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections are managed by city gas distribution companies and follow a different process.
PAHAL (DBTL) subsidy disbursement timelines and amounts are not covered.
